content.text: NASA is preparing to launch Artemis II, sending four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the Moon — the first crewed deep-space mission since Apollo 17 in 1972. The flight will ride on the Space Launch System, a 322-foot-tall rocket that generates 8.8 million pounds of thrust at liftoff using four RS-25 engines and two solid rocket boosters. This is currently the only vehicle capable of carrying a crewed Orion spacecraft into lunar vicinity at speeds over 36,000 km/h.
